Welcome to my website!
Please feel free to browse to learn more about my campaign and my commitment to serving Pleasanton and the Tri-Valley.
My husband and I have called Pleasanton home for 30 years. We raised our two daughters here, where they each graduated from the Pleasanton school district and went on to earn college degrees.
I grew up in a family where civic service was modeled by both of my parents. Mine started as a member of the Parks and Recreation Commission for 5 years followed by 5 years on the Planning Commission. When a special election was called to fill former Mayor Thorne’s City Council seat, I was strongly encouraged by members of the community to run for his vacant seat. Although I was nervous about the public speaking aspect, I did go ahead and run, and as they say, the rest is history.
During nearly a decade of service on the Pleasanton City Council, I served on the water subcommittee of the Council, as well as many others. At the end of my second term in 2022, I thought my public service was at an end. But then Zone 7 Water Agency, the Tri-Valley water wholesaler, had an opening on their Board and I was encouraged to apply given my work on water issues while on the council. I was appointed to the Board and served out the remainder of the term, then successfully ran for election in March 2024. I’ve been a member of the finance committee and just concluded a term as President of the Board of Directors.
Given my time on Zone 7, I have the unique perspective of having both sides of the water story—from the wholesale side to the retail side—both with the ultimate goal of delivering clean water reliably to Tri-Valley residents.
It was a difficult decision to consider not finishing my term on Zone 7, but I believe that my experience there has given me an even deeper understanding of water issues that I can now use to our community benefit as a councilmember. The Zone 7 staff have been amazing to work with and the Board is highly competent with an excellent mix of backgrounds. Given that, along with a couple of excellent potential candidates to take my place, I was comfortable in my decision to run for City Council District 1.
Not only do I have deep experience in water issues, but I also serve on three nonprofit boards and have a firm foundation of how they work and benefit our community. In early 2023, I joined the Board of Sunflower Hill and the Pleasanton Downtown Assoc. I also serve on the PPIE Board, the educational foundation for the school district.
Since my service on the City Council, I have chaired the PUSD Budget Advisory Committee, and I currently chair the Citizens Bond Oversight Committee, as well as the 7-11 Committee, because we know that high-quality schools are essential for our students and their families in our community.
I’m running for City Council in District 1 (https://www.cityofpleasantonca.gov/assets/our-government/city-clerk/District-map-streets.pdf) because residents deserve to be represented by someone who is experienced, accessible, does their homework and is an effective leader.
I am committed to helping protect what makes our community special while preparing it for a vibrant and sustainable future.
I’m also committed to mentoring district residents who might be interested in serving on the Council but don’t know where to begin because I have a responsibility to mentor potential future residents to serve on the City Council.
I invite you to browse my website. If you have any questions or comments, please email me at narumkathy@gmail.com
I would love to earn your support.
Warmly,
Kathy Narum
